__comment__: POSITION STAYS [0,0,0]. A bone animation's position is applied in the bone's
OWN ROTATED frame, so a lift combined with a rotation slides the model sideways
instead of up. The hand height is baked into the GEOMETRY instead (cubes shifted
so the centre sits at y=22, pivot [0,22,0]), the way Microsoft's wrench sample
does it. Geometry coordinates are never rotated, so that offset holds.
FIRST PERSON AND THIRD PERSON NEED DIFFERENT Y ROTATIONS.
The two views look at the hand bone from about 90 degrees apart, so a single Y
value cannot show a flat face in both. That is exactly why there are two
first person  Y=215 showed the CAMERA face-on -> screen needs 215-180 = 35
third person  Y=215 showed the phone EDGE-ON  -> a face needs 215-90  = 125
wrong side toward you ....... add or subtract 180 from rotation[1]
showing its edge, not a face  add or subtract 90 from rotation[1]
held too upright / stiff .... make rotation[0] more negative (more tilt)
too big or small ............ change scale
